counterevidence_considered.description: The input table does contain repeated rows per independent unit (three sessions per collar, 36 rows total), and the report mentions the 36-row count, so the precondition for the issue class exists in the raw data. However, this is neutralized because the code path feeds only the 12 collar means into the test, and the reported U and p are reproducible only from those 12 values (a row-level test on 36 values would have a maximum U of 324, far above the reported U = 35).
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: 36 session rows exist but do not enter the test

source_refs.quoted_text: Twelve permanent chamber collars were installed in a boreal fen: six in intact peat and six inside an experimental drainage block. Each collar was revisited in three seasonal flux sessions, so the source table holds 36 measurement rows for 12 collars.

evidence.description: The data description names collar_id as the independent unit and states one row is one seasonal session, so each collar contributes three repeated rows.
evidence.observed_value: independent unit = collar_id; 3 session rows per collar; 36 rows for 12 collars

source_refs.quoted_text:
One row is: one seasonal chamber flux session measured at one permanent collar
Independent unit column: collar_id

evidence.description: The workflow collapses each collar's three session rows to a single analysed value (the mean of its session fluxes) before any test is applied.
evidence.observed_value: collapse_to_collars computes one mean_flux per collar via fmean

source_refs.quoted_text:
def collapse_to_collars(grouped):

evidence.description: In main(), mannwhitneyu is called only on the collar-level mean fluxes returned by group_means (six intact and six drained values), not on the 36 session rows.
evidence.observed_value: test input = 12 collar means (6 per treatment)

source_refs.quoted_text:
collars = collapse_to_collars(grouped)
    flux = group_means(collars)
    test = mannwhitneyu(

evidence.description: The report states the test was run on the 12 collar-level mean fluxes with the collar as the independent unit, and its reported statistics (U = 35, exact two-sided p = 0.004329) are exactly reproduced by hand from the collar means: only one intact/drained pair is discordant (DRN-04 mean 12.30 exceeds INT-05 mean 11.80), giving U = 36 - 1 = 35, and the exact two-sided p is 2 x (2/924) = 4/924 = 0.004329. This confirms n = 12, not n = 36, entered the test.
evidence.observed_value: U = 35, p = 4/924 = 0.004329 from 12 collar means; matches report

source_refs.quoted_text:
A two-sided exact Mann-Whitney U test was run on the 12 collar-level mean fluxes, six per treatment, with the collar as the independent unit. The exact null distribution is used because the group sizes are small and no collar mean is tied.

U = 35, exact two-sided p = 0.004329, common-language effect size = 0.972 (the probability that a randomly chosen intact collar exceeds a randomly chosen drained collar).

[selected-result] Collar-mean CH4 flux was higher in intact fen than in drained fen (exact two-sided Mann-Whitney U = 35, n = 6 vs 6 collars, p = 0.004329; group means 14.00 vs 9.10 mg m^-2 h^-1, difference 4.90).

evidence.description: Collar-mean values in the report table match manual recomputation from the raw CSV rows (e.g., INT-01: (13.1+14.8+14.7)/3 = 14.20; DRN-06: (6.2+7.5+7.0)/3 = 6.90), confirming the collapse was performed as described.
evidence.observed_value: INT-01 mean 14.20 and DRN-06 mean 6.90 match report table

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to show the issue was present by tracing every path from the 36-row input to the mannwhitneyu call: read_sessions groups rows by collar, collapse_to_collars reduces each collar to one mean, and group_means passes exactly six values per treatment to the test, so no session-level rows can reach it. I then tried to falsify the report's numbers by independent recomputation: from the raw CSV I recomputed all 12 collar means (matching the report table), counted discordant intact/drained pairs (exactly one: DRN-04 12.30 > INT-05 11.80) giving U = 35, and computed the exact two-sided p as 4/924 = 0.004329, both matching the report. A pseudoreplicated 36-row test would produce a U statistic on a 18x18 = 324 scale, inconsistent with the reported U = 35 on the 6x6 = 36 scale. All falsification attempts failed, supporting the no-issue verdict.
